U1.boundary: Complex written input: locating, structuring and interpreting information. Do not turn content vocabulary, reference devices or isolated grammar rows into unrelated production targets.
U1.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 main-point/detail reading, paragraph cohesion, instruction following and reference tracking without relabelling them as new B2 content.
U1.cross_cutting: X-DISCOURSE, X-REFERENCE; register/stance only where the source task requires them.

U2.boundary: Argument, stance and implication in written input. Keep recognition of persuasion/tone/position distinct from independent argumentative production until later units.
U2.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 viewpoint recognition, reason/result links and text organisation.

U3.boundary: Extended listening and multi-modal interpretation. Pronunciation cues support perception and intelligibility; they are not accent-perfection targets or three isolated pronunciation lessons.
U3.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 main-point/detail listening, familiar-speaker repair and note-selection skills.
U3.cross_cutting: X-REFERENCE and X-DISCOURSE through source tracking; pronunciation is perception-first where appropriate.

U4.boundary: Detailed spoken description, explanation, procedure and narrative. Broad descriptive lexis is contextual/support unless later Stage-8 evidence requires independent production; grammar rows must stay grouped into functional systems.
U4.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 connected description, sequencing, narrative time and explanation while extending detail, precision and sustained turn length.
U4.cross_cutting: X-DISCOURSE, X-REFERENCE, X-PRAGMATICS plus intelligibility-focused pronunciation.

U5.boundary: Supported viewpoint, evaluation, probability and speculation. Keep certainty, modal, hypothetical and comparison resources meaning-bounded; do not make one grammar rule per EGP row.
U5.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 opinion/reason support, comparison and basic modal/conditional foundations without reteaching them as new.

U6.boundary: Collaborative discussion and spontaneous contribution. Language resources serve turn management, precision, disagreement and repair; scripted model reproduction cannot substitute for spontaneous evidence.
U6.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 conversation management, agreeing/disagreeing, clarification and repair in less predictable exchanges.
U6.cross_cutting: X-PRAGMATICS, X-STANCE, X-DISCOURSE; pronunciation supports turn-taking and comprehensibility.

U7.boundary: Problems, complaints, negotiation and resolution. Keep request/obligation/politeness forms tied to interpersonal effect and outcome; avoid decontextualised transformation practice as the evidence target.
U7.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 problem description, requests, suggestions and practical resolution language under greater pressure and detail.

U8.boundary: Formal discussion, interview, survey and presentation Q&A. Formality is audience/task-sensitive, not a list of formal synonyms; prepared presentation cannot substitute for responsive Q&A evidence.
U8.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 prepared speaking and question handling, then extend precision, follow-up and register control.
U8.cross_cutting: X-REGISTER, X-PRAGMATICS, X-DISCOURSE; pronunciation supports sustained formal interaction.

U9.boundary: Mediation, relay, paraphrase, synthesis and facilitation. Preserve source stance and recipient need; mediation is not verbatim copying and is not proof of unrestricted independent production of every source form.
U9.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 summary/relay and clarification skills with denser sources and more explicit recipient adaptation.

U10.boundary: Detailed descriptive, explanatory, procedural and narrative writing. Broad lexical coverage remains contextual/support pending Stage 8; dense reference/noun-phrase grammar must serve text clarity rather than become a multi-rule grammar chapter.
U10.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 connected paragraphing, sequencing, description/narrative and editing while extending length, detail and information density.
U10.cross_cutting: X-REFERENCE, X-DISCOURSE, X-REGISTER where genre requires it.

U11.boundary: Written argument, evaluation and source-informed synthesis. Issue vocabulary may remain receptive/contextual; evidence requires reasoning, source relationship and audience adaptation rather than lexical display.
U11.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 opinion paragraphs, reasons/examples and basic comparison while extending counter-position, evidence and synthesis.

U12.boundary: Correspondence, online collaboration, reports and reviews. Preserve distinct genre success conditions; formal/content vocabulary exposure does not make every word a productive target.
U12.b1_carry_forward: Retrieve B1 audience/register, practical correspondence and structured factual writing while extending interaction chains and standalone genres.

U13.boundary: Cumulative exit evidence only. These six slots introduce no required B2 source record; they sample previously taught capabilities under changed topics, audiences, speakers, sources and reduced model dependence.
U13.b1_carry_forward: Sample retained B1 foundations only as prerequisites inside integrated B2 performance; do not relabel or reteach them as B2 inventory.
U13.cross_cutting: All relevant cross-cutting resources are sampled role-appropriately; no new system, phrase, lexical target or pronunciation strand is introduced.
